benchmarks: T1 codebase-notes corpus (29 docs/100 questions), T2 corporate corpus (68 docs/50 questions), scaling corpus (3600 Russian Wikipedia articles, CC BY-SA); baseline = Graphiti/Zep (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Q4_K_M)
fallos_mitigaciones: Baseline (Graphiti) LLM-extraction produced fabrications (distorted entity names, mixed-language facts absent from input, S3.2) -- mitigated by fully deterministic non-generative write path (zero LLM calls). Naive write-path implementation degrades superlinearly with ghost-edge count (166->846ms, 5.1x at 3600 docs, S3.3) -- mitigated by schema migration (generated column+partial indexes, GIN on aliases, journal indexes, OR->UNION ALL rewrite), achieving 107->147ms (1.4x) and 3.7x ingest speedup at 3600 docs with identical edge semantics.

notes: S2.1-2.2: Markdown git-repo = source of truth; write=atomic git-commit+PG16 transaction; derived layers (FTS russian morphology, bge-m3 dense vectors/pgvector HNSW, doc-graph w/ wiki-links+auto 'ghost' mentions) fully rebuildable, ZERO generative LLM calls on write path vs Graphiti/Zep baseline (~500 LLM calls, 2h04min vs ~10s for 68 docs). S2.1 'quarantine of trust': new/changed docs 'under review' until human-confirmed before reaching generative consumers -> FIDELIDAD.
